requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
**Implementation.** The only `{impl}` site is `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`. It is marked by the `:impl:` anchor on the requirement in `md/requirements/cli.md`. The file carries out each obligation in the requirement text:

- **Bundled.** The skill sits under `assets/skills`, which the `Cargo.toml` Symposium skills metadata publishes. It has proper front matter with a name and description.
- **Read the code and tests.** It tells agents to "Read the project's existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests" and to "Follow behavior through the code".
- **Map every first-party test.** The first inventory covers "Every first-party runnable test or test case", including integration tests, doctests and parameterized cases. It requires at least one `{test}` reference on each test definition or case, naming a full requirement or example. It forbids using a file-level tag to stand in for unrelated tests.
- **Map every source unit with end-user-visible behavior.** The second inventory covers every explicit function or method in first-party Rust sources. It also covers public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors and distinct observable branches. It says not to count one tagged entry point as coverage for deeper code. Each item gets an `{impl}`, `{test}` or `{cite}` reference by the reference procedure, or a fenced `habeas:none` with a justification. It says an item citing `habeas:none` must not implement end-user-observable behavior that no requirement specifies.
- **Report gaps and claim completeness only after independent review.** It says to "Have both inventories independently reviewed against the source and tests before claiming complete coverage". It also says to "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items". Finally, it says to "List remaining gaps with file locations and reasons; do not invent evidence or silently exclude difficult cases".

The skill also contains user-review, authoring-harness and reference-procedure guidance that this requirement does not mention. Other requirements specify it, and each marks this file with `:impl:`: `requirements_review_skill`, `behavior_review_guidance`, `internal_detail_guidance` and `authoring.batch`. So the file carries no unspecified behavior. No other code implements this requirement without an `{impl}` marker, because the deliverable is the skill document itself.

**Tests.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs::bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories` is the main test.
- It parses `Cargo.toml` and asserts that a Symposium skills entry has source path `assets/skills`.
- It checks the skill's front matter.
- It asserts exact phrases for each obligation: reading code and tests, mapping tests, mapping source units, and independent review with gap reporting.

The helpers `bundled_skill` and `assert_phrases` are also marked `{test}`. Phrase matching is a suitable way to test a prose document. The test fails if any directive is removed or weakened. Other tests (`bundled_skills_direct_*`, `bundled_skills_require_agreed_requirements_before_code`) add checks on the same file through their own requirements. The phrase checks do not verify that an agent would behave correctly, but nothing more is practical for a static guidance document.

No gaps and no FIXMEs were found.
